scope: Research and hardware experiment design; no executable EBR behavior and no completed hardware measurements

hardware_policy.decision: Unresolved behavior and source disagreements are queued for tests on the user's ECP5-85F board; continue collecting other resources meanwhile
hardware_policy.evidence_rule: Retain exact configuration and observation; reproducibility on one device does not establish a universal outcome for vendor-undefined collisions

rules.subject: core_clock_enable
rules.claim: clken gates read and write in the Yosys memory contract

rules.subject: sync_reset_priority
rules.claim: Yosys DP sync reset zero has priority over clock/read enables

rules.subject: sync_reset_write
rules.claim: Yosys uses native synchronous reset only when write and reset are proved mutually exclusive; otherwise it emulates reset in fabric. This does not establish hardware reset-versus-write priority.

rules.subject: async_reset_write
rules.claim: rdarst zero resets the read result; this declaration supplies no general asynchronous write-blocking rule

rules.subject: byte_write
rules.claim: Yosys wrbe_separate writes a group only when CLK_EN, WR_EN and its WR_BE bit are one

rules.subject: read_write_new
rules.claim: Yosys rdwr new means the whole new memory word, including unchanged groups of a masked write; this is not a chip measurement

rules.subject: cross_port_priority
rules.claim: The ECP5 Yosys library declares neither wrprio nor wrtrans; no cross-port priority or read transparency is supplied

rules.subject: initial_read_output
rules.claim: Yosys rdinit zero declares an initial read value; actual configuration/startup behavior still needs a board test

rules.subject: output_clock_enable
rules.claim: Memory guide output-clock-enable selection requires the optional output register

rules.subject: reset_release
rules.claim: Memory guide distinguishes synchronous and asynchronous release of asynchronous reset, but does not specify the internal edge count or its complete enable priority

rules.subject: reset_contents
rules.claim: Reset preserves the memory array; FAQ 3626 additionally describes reset as applying to output registers

rules.subject: raw_cs
rules.claim: CSDECODE from the bitstream already includes the writer's source-level CS inversion; compare reverse3(decoded_word) with raw CS
